nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox testing costs

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: a single undifferentiated 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE available. No real roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, PM) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet. All costs below are indicative only and must be revisited once actual team members, roles and rates are confirmed — true costs could differ substantially depending on seniority mix and specialisation.

No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project or team; estimate is built from story points translated to engineering hours using a standard assumption of ~8 hours of effort per story point (a common, though rough, translation used absent velocity data), which is itself a source of uncertainty.

Only 1 FTE is available against a backlog totalling 189 story points (~1512 base hours of implementation), which is a substantial mismatch: at 1 FTE working full-time this backlog represents over a year of solo work. Additional buffer hours (~63% on top of base) have been added for integration, testing, code review substitutes, rework and project management overhead that would normally be spread across multiple roles/people — this inflates the single-person hour estimate to 2,464 hours. This is flagged explicitly: the role is staffed far too thinly for the backlog it must absorb, and realistically this project requires multiple FTEs/roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, DevOps) to be delivered in a reasonable timeframe.

Story points were mapped to hours per item based on relative complexity described (e.g. legacy data migration at 21 points assumed to require significant hours for schema mapping, batch processing and validation; simple CRUD-style features at 5 points assumed to require comparatively less effort), then summed and multiplied by an effort-buffer factor for a single generalist absorbing all disciplines.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for Stripe sandbox/integration testing, migration tooling/licensing for the legacy Oracle extract, and minor infra costs for CI/staging — these have not been quoted from vendors and should be confirmed.
Priority-based cost breakdown is derived pro-rata from each task's estimated hours/cost relative to total backlog cost, grouped by the priority label given in the backlog.

Scenario range (10th/50th/90th percentile) reflects overall estimation uncertainty given the placeholder rate card, unproven single-person velocity, and lack of historical actuals; the pessimistic scenario also accounts for high-risk items (legacy migration, payment integration, RBAC) running over.

It is assumed the team member is a generalist capable of covering full-stack development, QA, DevOps and coordination tasks, which is optimistic and a key risk factor if only one person is truly available.
input.reasoning: Backlog was translated into effort using story points as a proxy for relative complexity, converted to hours (~8 hrs/point baseline) and then inflated by a buffer (~63%) to account for the fact that a single 'Team member' FTE must cover all disciplines (design, build, test, deploy, PM) that would normally be split across specialised roles. This produced a total of 2,464 hours at the placeholder rate of $75/hr = $184,800 in labour. Non-labour costs were added for third-party/integration costs tied to specific backlog items (Stripe fees, Oracle migration tooling, CI/staging infra). Three scenarios were produced to reflect the wide uncertainty inherent in: (a) a placeholder, unvalidated rate card; (b) no historical actuals; and (c) a severe capacity mismatch (1 FTE vs ~189 points of backlog). The priority breakdown apportions the labour+non-labour cost pro-rata across each task's priority tag so the client can see where budget concentration lies (Urgent/High priority items like auth, RBAC, payments and migration dominate risk and cost). Cost-reduction recommendations focus on descoping/deferring Low-priority items, trimming Medium-priority scope, and flagging the single-FTE capacity constraint as the primary lever/risk for both cost and schedule.

reductions.description: Defer all 5 Low-priority backlog items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase/backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes ~39 points / ~266 buffered hours of scope from the current estimate; legacy portal can typically keep running a little longer and support/analytics/back-office tooling can follow after the core customer-facing portal ships.

reductions.description: Descope or simplify Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) to a single-currency (USD-only) launch, deferring EUR/PLN settlement and daily FX handling.
reductions.effect: Cuts a large Medium-priority item down to near-zero incremental work for v1; multi-currency can be added once real customer demand for EUR/PLN is confirmed.

reductions.description: Reduce Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope for launch to critical-path screens only (registration, login, dashboard, payments) rather than full WCAG 2.2 AA coverage across all screens, with full coverage as a fast-follow.
reductions.effect: Lowers initial effort on an 8-point item while still meeting compliance on the highest-traffic/highest-risk flows; remaining screens addressed in a subsequent iteration.

reductions.description: Increase team capacity beyond the current 1 FTE placeholder (e.g. add a second team member or contractor) rather than trying to compress the single-FTE timeline.
reductions.effect: Does not reduce total dollar cost, but is flagged as the key structural fix: 1 FTE against ~189 points of backlog implies a very long delivery timeline and higher risk of rework/context-switching costs that are not fully captured in this dollar estimate. Recommend re-costing once real roles/rates are known.
